panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Head CT bone window from a patient with Hunter syndrome shows the captioned enlarged/partially empty sella turcica, a recognized mucopolysaccharidosis cranial manifestation. B: Axial soft tissue CT shows captioned bilateral scleral thickening and microphthalmia, reported in this case as an unusual ocular manifestation of Hunter syndrome; no skin is assessable. C: Axial soft tissue head CT from the Hunter syndrome case shows captioned prominent perivascular spaces, an intracranial mucopolysaccharidosis finding. D: Sagittal soft tissue CT shows captioned sellar enlargement and mega cisterna magna, consistent with intracranial stigmata of Hunter syndrome. E: Axial soft tissue head CT from the Hunter syndrome case shows captioned ventriculomegaly. F: Axial soft tissue head CT shows captioned diffuse white matter abnormalities and prominent perivascular spaces in the Hunter syndrome patient.

in_text_mentions: 36-year-old man with no relevant family history was diagnosed with Hunter syndrome at nine years of age (with iduronate sulfatase level of 0.0 mmol/L/ml (normal range 105-262) and urinary GAG level of 42 mg/mmol creatinine (normal range 1-5)). He was referenced to our center at the age of 23, presenting symptoms such as short stature (1.42 m), short limbs, enlarged head, coarse facial features (broad nose and lower face with flared nostrils, thickened lips, irregular, and peg-shaped teeth) (Figure 1), broad thickened hands (Figure 2) with stubby digits, and dysostosis multiplex (Figures 3, 4).
